A private, fast home screen with an optional assistant that runs on your phone.

No accounts, ads, analytics or crash reporting, and no server of ours: there is nothing for this app to send your data to. Online features (weather, news, downloads…) are off until you turn each one on, and they talk only to the services named in Settings → Online features.

Turns what you say into text, entirely on this phone. Whisper (open source, whisper.cpp) works on any phone and is often more accurate; the phone\'s recognizer starts a little faster.

Say your wake word to open the assistant, hands-free. A tiny open-source model listens for that phrase only; nothing else is recognised, kept or sent. Android shows a notification and the green mic dot while it listens. Uses some battery.
For fewer false wakes and better accent coverage, a Whisper model double-checks what was said. Whisper tiny is enough (%1$s).

A private home screen: no accounts, no ads, no analytics, and no server of ours. Online extras like the weather stay off until you turn them on.
Swipe up anywhere on the home screen to see every app. Press Home to come back.
Tap the search bar and type a few letters: \"gm\" finds Google Maps. Press Go to open the first app, or search the web with DuckDuckGo or another engine you choose in Settings.
Long-press any app and choose Hide, or Hide and lock to protect it with your fingerprint or PIN. Find them again in Settings → Hidden apps.
The home screen learns which apps you open at different times and days, and suggests them. It\'s all worked out on this phone. Turn it off or forget the history in Settings.

Optional, and it runs on this phone. Tap ✦ or hold the power button: \"call Jen\", \"set an alarm for 7\", \"when I say goodnight, play rain sounds\". It always asks before texting, calling or booking.
